title: Advanced pulmonary function test parameters and clinical relevance
summary: The study uses existing routine pulmonary function tests (body plethysmography and spirometry) from 2021–2025, to examine whether “advanced” parameters—such as inspiratory reserve volume, intrathoracic gas volume, or the area under the flow-volume curve—are useful in daily practice. The study will analyze at least 385 patients with obstructive lung diseases (COPD/asthma), 385 patients with restrictive lung diseases, and at least 385 patients with mixed ventilatory disorders. The goal is to determine which of these additional parameters are particularly meaningful for diagnosis, monitoring treatment, or predicting disease progression—and thereby improve clinical decision-making. All data will be anonymized and evaluated exclusively within the University Hospital, so no new consent from the patients is required.
conditions: Obstructive, restrictive, and mixed ventilatory disorders

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients with obstruction, restriction, mixed ventilatory dysfunction, and normal pulmonary function test results.
Exclusion criteria:
• Acute infection and signs of exacerbation
• Patients whose pulmonary function tests do not meet the inclusion criteria (Section 1.2.3) and who demonstrated inadequate coordination or cooperation during the examination
• Patients who have undergone surgery within the past 1 month
